title: Implement versioned symbol stubs and delayed resolution for mixed Cutlass/Triton runtimes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: mixed deployed fleets and developer machines are running combinations of CUDA (11/12/13), Triton versions and multiple CUTLASS releases. At startup and during live upgrades we see symbol resolution races, heavy full-probe paths that add 40-150ms of tail latency to cold starts, and occasional ABI mismatch crashes when newer kernels expose symbols not present in older system libs. Current mitigations (fat-bundles, environment pinning, ad-hoc ifdefs) are brittle and increase build matrix and image size.

Proposal: introduce a lightweight, versioned symbol stub layer and delayed-resolution loader: 1) during build we generate small symbol stubs with annotated compatibility metadata (compat-version, fallback-level) for exported kernel entry points; 2) at runtime the loader maps stubs but defers heavy probe/resolution until first use of each symbol (lazy binding). When the real vendor symbol is missing or incompatible we resolve to a pinned fallback implementation (bundled or software) and emit a structured event for observability. The loader includes an opt-in strict-mode that fails fast on missing critical symbols for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Goals: reduce cold-start probe latency, shrink effective runtime probe surface, provide deterministic controlled fallbacks for mixed fleets, and simplify the build matrix by enabling a single multi-variant artifact with runtime resolution policy.

Scope: runtime loader changes, build-time stub generator, CI changes for symbol verification, unit + integration + stress tests, benchmark dashboards, RFC approval, 10% canary rollout and automatic rollback policy.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start median probe latency reduced by >= 25% across representative models compared to baseline (see perf dashboard).
No increase in 95th percentile token latency during steady-state workloads after canary rollout (<= 5% change).
Deterministic fallback exercised and logged when a missing symbol occurs; logs must include symbol name, requested version, chosen fallback, and host id.
Unit tests and compatibility matrix added to CI covering (CUDA11-13) x (Triton2-3) x (CUTLASS variants).
Feature gated behind runtime flag 'enable_versioned_stubs' and strict-mode flag 'strict_kernel_resolution' for enterprise customers.
technical_notes: Stub format: ELF .symstub section with metadata blob (text key:value pairs) and a small trampoline for lazy bind.
Loader flow: premap stubs at module load, register lazy resolver callbacks, resolve on first-call with timeout; if unresolved after 200ms, fall back to bundled implementation and emit event.
Compatibility model: semantic integer version + minor compatibility bitmask; build-time generator computes best-match fallback pack for each artifact.

Performance trade-offs: lazy bind adds a one-time first-call latency; we offset with aggressive prefix/KV cache warming and synthetic warmup calls for common kernels during container bootstrap for Dedicated pools.
Security: stubs validated via signature over metadata and symbol list. Security team requested threat model doc (see links).
comments: 2025-11-07 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after two regressions in weekend deploys where mixed Triton/CUTLASS combos caused startup crashes. Attached initial perf traces and native crashes from kube nodes.
2025-11-09 Marco Ruiz: Added initial impl plan. Prototype of stub generator in runtime/loader/experimental/; local perf shows 38ms median improvement on small-model cold path (w/ warmup disabled).

2025-11-10 Dan Huang (Reviewer): Concern about first-call latency spikes for rare heavy kernels. Suggested deterministic synthetic warmup for top-50 kernels and observed fallback metric instrumentation. Marked for follow-up work.
2025-11-11 CI: Symbol verification jobs added to nightly; discovered two symbols with ambiguous versions in CUTLASS-3.2 build artifacts — added mapping table and updated generator.

2025-11-12 QA: Ran 12h soak in staging with feature flag enabled on 5-node cluster. Observed 0.6% increase in first-token latency for a subset of scripts, but 28% reduction in startup probe time. Captured logs for fallback events.
2025-11-13 Security review: requested signed metadata and stricter verification for Private deployments. Added security review doc link and toggles for strict-mode.

2025-11-14 Ops: Rolling canary started in us-west2 at 03:00 UTC (10% of runtime fleets). Early telemetry: fallback events at 0.02% host-call rate; queued follow-up to add richer tags (model_id, customer_tier).

2025-11-15 Marco Ruiz: Canaries stable after 24h. Preparing PR to remove experimental flag behind 'enable_versioned_stubs' default=false. Next: add CI permutations and schedule enterprise rollout doc.
notes: Rollout plan: feature-flagged opt-in -> 10% canary -> 50% -> full. Observe: startup probe time, first-call latency histograms, fallback event rate. Revert criteria: >1% service errors OR >5% increase in 95p token latency. Follow-ups: generator convex-optimization to minimize fallback footprint, add automatic kernel warmup in Dedicated startup path.
